profiles.summary: No opcode result differs from the specification at Monad/0.16.7 on 2026-11-26. All 185,529 vectors match, and script sets 1, 2 and 6 differ from Ethereum only at the same heavy swaps and at address 0x1000 as before. New this cycle: the VM sources of v0.16.6 equal those of v0.16.7 file for file, v0.16.6 is marked as skippable, and the main branch now carries unreleased rewrites of the integer library and the x86 emitter that no tag contains.

deltas.delta: The jsDelivr file hashes of the tags show 28 VM, interpreter, compiler and integer library files changed from v0.16.5 to v0.16.6 and none from v0.16.6 to v0.16.7. The changed set includes emitter.cpp (shift_literal_by_non_literal, the once-per-element memory bound check, the stack-exit writes and branchless CLZ), uint256.hpp (countl_zero only), the interpreter's execute.cpp, stack.hpp and a new stack_top.hpp. Cycle 23 ran the PoolManager natively and in the interpreter at v0.16.5 and v0.16.7, so this whole delta is already under test.

The v0.16.6 upgrade page says the version can be skipped in favour of v0.16.7. The v0.16.7 page still says its instructions apply to testnet only, and the release page lists v0.16.7 for testnet on 2026-11-19 with mainnet N/A, and v0.16.5 for mainnet on 2026-10-22. rpc.monad.xyz, rpc1.monad.xyz and rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com all answered Monad/0.16.7 on 2026-11-26.

Main differs from v0.16.7 in 92 files under category/vm and category/core/runtime. uint256.hpp grows from 37,912 to 75,879 bytes and adds a Barrett reduction for udivrem, addmod, mulmod and mulmod by a constant. No VM file on main calls it: of the 109 header and source files under category/vm and category/core/runtime, only uint256.hpp contains the words barrett or reciprocal, and runtime/math.hpp still calls the division-based mulmod. The division-based udivrem now denormalises only the n significant words of the remainder and zero-fills the rest, which gives the same words because Knuth division leaves the higher words zero.

The emitter on main keeps a per-block touched_memory_end_ for literal memory offsets and skips the bound check and the call to the memory growth routine when a later MLOAD or MSTORE at a literal offset ends at or below it (emitter.cpp lines 6340-6356). The value resets at every block entry that is a jump destination (lines 1030-1045). It moves to the asmjit 2 API, calls runtime functions through an immediate address instead of a read-only data slot, and moves the CALLDATALOAD partial-word handlers to the end of the contract. None of this is in a tag.

findings.title: Monad's main branch rewrites the integer library and the x86 emitter in ways that would reach compiled PoolManager blocks before any eth_call can see them
findings.difference: Monad validators run native code that the x86 emitter produces for frequently used contracts, while every public endpoint answers eth_call and serves traces through the interpreter. The main branch, which no tag carries, changes that emitter and the 256 bit library in four places: a Barrett reduction for division, ADDMOD and MULMOD in uint256.hpp, elision of the memory bound check for literal offsets already touched in the block, direct calls to runtime routines by immediate address, and a migration to the asmjit 2 API.
findings.mechanism: The PoolManager's pool math runs MULMOD with the literal modulus 2^256-1 on every mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24) and with a variable modulus for the low remainder (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:48, :112, src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:252). A Barrett path for a constant modulus, if a later release wired it into the MULMOD handler, would sit under all of these. Today no VM file on main calls it, and math.hpp still calls the division-based mulmod. The literal-offset memory elision on main applies to the revert encoders and the free memory pointer (src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:16-43, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:144, src/types/Currency.sol:57), which write at offsets 0x00, 0x04 and 0x40. The emitter resets the tracked end at every block that is a jump destination, and memory never shrinks within a frame, so on reading the elision gives the same result. A wrong elision would read or write memory past the frame's allocation. The interpreter would not show it, because eth_call never runs native code (rpc/monad_executor.cpp lines 1306-1309 at v0.16.7), and tracing nodes run the interpreter for blocks too (cmd/monad/main.cpp line 488). A fault would show only as the tracing RPC nodes falling out of consensus at the delayed merkle root, three blocks later. By then the validators' result is canonical.
findings.impact: None today. No release contains these changes and no revision after MONAD_TEN is scheduled. If a release carried a fault in one of these paths and two thirds of validators ran it, every pool's swap and liquidity amounts would follow the faulty native result.
findings.preconditions: Monad must tag and roll out a release built from main, and a fault must exist on a path the PoolManager reaches. An ordinary swap would then trigger it. No ordinary account can make validators run a given release.
findings.mitigations: When a tag after v0.16.7 appears, rebuild the cycle 23 harness (cycles/023/theme-monad-compiled-coverage.work/tools/build.sh) at that tag. Run the six script sets and the mined transactions natively, and run a direct test of uint256.hpp's mulmod, addmod and udivrem, with the Barrett variants, against Python integers. Do this before validators adopt the tag.

cleared.check: Whether v0.16.6 runs different VM code from v0.16.5 or v0.16.7.
cleared.result: The jsDelivr file hashes show no file under category/vm, category/core/runtime or the execution state paths changed from v0.16.6 to v0.16.7. v0.16.6 differs from v0.16.5 in 28 such files, which is the delta cycle 23 compiled and ran at v0.16.7. The v0.16.6 upgrade page says the version can be skipped. A validator on v0.16.6 therefore runs the VM that the cycle 23 harness tested at v0.16.7.

cleared.check: shift_literal_by_non_literal in the v0.16.6 and v0.16.7 emitter, used by the tick bitmap masks shl(and(tick,0xff),1) and 1 << bitPos (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:73, :110), read again line by line.
cleared.result: For SHL, the 96-byte table holds 7 as the bit mask, 32 zero bytes, then the value. The window load at value minus k bytes and the carry load one byte lower are shifted per 64-bit lane by b bits, and the carry is moved right by 8. With the count clamped to 256, this gives bit i of lane j equal to bit 64j+i-8k-b of the value for every count from 0 to 256. SHR and SAR use value, fill, fill words, the mask at offset 80, and the mirror image of this rule. The fill is all ones for a negative literal under SAR. The highest byte any load reaches is the first byte of the third word, which holds fill. Cycle 16 ran 46 micro programs per shape and a planted fault on this path. The reading agrees with them.

cleared.check: The once-per-element memory bound check of v0.16.6 (emitter.cpp lines 6301-6313 at v0.16.7).
cleared.result: The check is skipped only when the same stack element, holding the same offset, already passed a check for at least the same read size in the same compiled block. Memory never shrinks within a frame, and a failed first check leaves the frame. So the skip never admits an access the full check would refuse, and it never omits an expansion charge, which is zero for memory already allocated. Cycle 23 ran the PoolManager natively at v0.16.7 with this code and found no difference from the interpreter.

cleared.check: Whether the Barrett reduction added to uint256.hpp on main reaches any EVM opcode handler.
cleared.result: It does not. Of 109 VM and runtime files on main, only uint256.hpp contains it. The mulmod that runtime/math.hpp calls is the division-based one (uint256.hpp lines 955-962 on main), and math.hpp changed only in an include and a revision constant. The udivrem change on main (the remainder is taken from the n significant words, and the rest is zero) gives the same words as v0.16.7, because Knuth division leaves the higher words of the normalised numerator zero.

cleared.check: Whether public endpoints and validators can disagree silently about a PoolManager result.
cleared.result: The public endpoints serve stored call frames (debug_traceTransaction with callTracer answered on rpc.monad.xyz, rpc1.monad.xyz and rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com on 2026-11-26), so they run --trace_calls and execute blocks with the interpreter (cmd/monad/main.cpp line 488 at v0.16.7). Monad's asynchronous execution page says a node whose delayed merkle root disagrees falls out of consensus and re-executes. rpc.monad.xyz served latest block 125,590,812 and finalized block 125,590,811, both at most one second old. Its interpreter state therefore agreed with the validator-voted roots at the tip that day. A divergence would stall the tracing fleet. It would not stay hidden.

cleared.check: Whether https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc executes blocks itself or applies the sequencer's results (L-1029).
cleared.result: The architecture page says replica nodes receive blocks and execution results from the sequencer and apply them without re-execution, and that this is the default RPC mode. The committed state on the endpoint is therefore the producer's write. A trace on the endpoint is the replica's own run of its mega-evm. The cycle 23 comparison of traced against committed state over 16,035 blocks was a check of the producer.

jsDelivr lists no version after 1.7.4. The ten files fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com on main equal those of v1.7.4 byte for byte. A jsDelivr data listing for @main disagrees with raw main: it names files raw main lacks, among them docs/spec/upgrades/rex7.md, and the CDN returns 404 for that file. The listing was not used as evidence.

leads.question: When a Monad tag after v0.16.7 appears, does it include main's Barrett reduction, literal-offset memory elision, immediate runtime calls or asmjit 2 migration? Run a direct test of that tag's uint256.hpp (mulmod, addmod, udivrem and each Barrett reciprocal range) against Python integers on FullMath-shaped inputs, and the cycle 23 native harness. This cycle's attempt to compile and run such a test locally was refused by the session's permission system before it ran.
leads.why: These paths would reach compiled PoolManager blocks first, and no RPC method can show them.

leads.question: Does asmjit 2 encode call imm(runtime_fun_) as a direct rel32 call only when the target is within 2 GiB of the JIT page, and through an address table otherwise, in the build Monad ships?
leads.why: A wrong relocation would send compiled PoolManager code to the wrong runtime routine, for example the MULMOD or EXP helper, on validators only.

leadResults.answer: On 2026-11-26 the release page still lists v0.16.5 as the last mainnet release and v0.16.7 as testnet only, while three public mainnet endpoints answer Monad/0.16.7. No tag after v0.16.7 exists. v0.16.6 is marked as skippable, and its VM files equal v0.16.7's. The VM delta from v0.16.5 to v0.16.7 (28 files) is the one cycle 23 compiled and ran at both tags without a difference. The newest 588 mined swaps (blocks 125,587,573 to 125,589,105) give the recorded results under swaps.py and replay.py. No release since v0.16.7 changes vm.cpp, the emitter or uint256.hpp. Main changes all three, unreleased. Which release each validator runs cannot be read from chain or from any public page.

The trigger has not occurred: no release after v0.16.5 has a mainnet date. The asmjit API migration is on main only, together with a rewritten uint256.hpp and new emitter changes. These are recorded as a new info finding and a lead for the first tag that carries them.

Second half: rpc.monad.xyz, rpc1.monad.xyz and rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com serve stored call frames to debug_traceTransaction. Stored frames exist only under --trace_calls, which selects VM::InterpreterOnly for block execution (cmd/monad/main.cpp line 488 at v0.16.7; the full node page recommends --trace_calls for RPC nodes). Committed-state comparisons on these endpoints are interpreter against interpreter. The link to validators is the delayed merkle root, and the endpoints were at the finalized tip on 2026-11-26. First half: basic_blocks.cpp did not change from v0.16.6 to v0.16.7, and EIP-8024 stays unscheduled. This half matters only for hooks once MONAD_NEXT_AMSTERDAM is scheduled, so it was not read again.

Not done this cycle. This unit checked the newest 5,955 MegaETH swaps through block 32,903,224, which runs past the cycle 23 window, with swaps.py and replay.py, and all match. It did not count PoolManager transactions in the stateless-validator blocks or measure their branch sides.
Operator-only ordering question. Nothing new is public: the resource limit specification still gives no order for reconsidering skipped candidates.

The architecture page says public RPC nodes are replicas by default and apply the sequencer's execution results without re-execution. The endpoint's committed state is the producer's, so the 16,035-block comparison of traced against committed state checked the producer.

The jsDelivr file hashes show that the VM, interpreter, compiler and integer library sources of v0.16.6 equal those of v0.16.7, and that they differ from v0.16.5 in the 28 files cycle 23 tested at v0.16.7. The v0.16.6 upgrade page says the version can be skipped in favour of v0.16.7. Whether a validator runs it cannot be read, and it would run the tested code if one did.
